newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium volatilities drift, zinc strong.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium volatilities drift, zinc strong.

text.p: LME aluminium option volatilities eased this week as buying of upside strikes subsided, futures drifted lower and light selling of forward dates emerged.
Zinc volatility edged higher, but volumes were modest throughout the options sector as the summer lull hit the market.
"Last week there was aggressive buying of $1,800 calls in aluminium, but that seems to have been fulfilled and the market is a bit long," one trader said.
"There was some selling of first quarter 1998, that helped ease vols in fourth quarter 1997," another said.
The volatility market often tracks the three months market, which lost about $50 this week to settle around the $1,700 mark, traders said.
September at-the-money (ATM) implied volatility was quoted on Friday morning at 21.0/24.0 percent, October at 22.5/24.5 percent, about two points down from a week ago.
One trader said a big off-market lump of $1,800 calls were granted mid-week, sending those vols down as low as 20 percent.
There was still a skew between calls and puts, with a two-point differential between a $1,600 put and a $1,800 call, another trader said.
In zinc, volatility ticked higher on renewed interest for nearbys, with players keen to load up on volatility ahead of September, where the tightness in futures is centred.
Strikes from $1,550 to $1,700 were in play.
"People are expecting further movement, either the spread to collapse or the spread to tighten -- more volatility," one dealer said.
Another said people were looking to pick up gamma through nearbys and sell vega on further forward dates.
September strangles were purchased for 46 percent volatility on Tuesday.
ATM September was quoted on Friday morning at 45.0/50.0 percent and October at 37.0/41.0 percent, up three to four points on the week.
Copper volatilities were little changed, with bits and pieces done.
ATM implied volatility for September was quoted at 22.5/25.0 percent and October at 21.75/23.00 percent.
Light buying of downside puts for the first half of 1998 was seen early in the week, with granting of nearby calls seen later in the week at $2,350 and $2,400 strikes for November and December.
Little activity was seen in the other metals.
